records.source: Θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ἡλίκον ἀγῶνα ἔχω ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ καὶ ὅσοι οὐχ ἑόρακαν τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ἐν σαρκί, ἵνα παρακληθῶσιν αἱ καρδίαι αὐτῶν, συμβιβασθέντες ἐν ἀγάπῃ καὶ εἰς πᾶν πλοῦτος τῆς πληροφορίας τῆς συνέσεως, εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ μυστηρίου τοῦ θεοῦ, Χριστοῦ, ἐν ᾧ εἰσιν πάντες οἱ θησαυροὶ τῆς σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως ἀπόκρυφοι.
records.gloss: I want for you to know how great a struggle I have on behalf of you and those in Laodicea and as many as have not seen the face of me in [the] flesh, \v 2 that may be encouraged the hearts of them, having been knit together in love and unto all [the] riches of the full assurance of the understanding, unto [the] knowledge of the mystery of the God, Christ, \v 3 in whom are all the treasures of the wisdom and knowledge hidden.
pieces: I want you to know how hard I am struggling for you, for those in Laodicea, and for everyone who has never met me in person.

My aim is that their hearts may be encouraged as they are joined together in love, and that they may have all the riches of understanding held with full confidence, so that they know God's mystery, which is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
In {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge lie hidden.

L.1: For I want you to know how great a struggle I have for you and for those in Laodicea and for all who have not seen my face in [the] flesh,
L.2: so that their hearts may be encouraged, being knit together in love and for all [the] riches of the full assurance of understanding, for [the] knowledge of the mystery of God, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.3: in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.

R.1: I want you to know how hard I am working and praying for you, for the believers in Laodicea, and for all who have never seen me face to face.
R.2: I want them to be encouraged and joined together in love. I want them to have the rich blessing of understanding fully and being completely sure. Then they will know God's mystery, which is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
R.3: All the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: a great struggle: hard effort and deep concern on their behalf, above all in prayer
decisions.reason: ἀγῶνα is the word for a contest, and picks up "struggling" at the end of chapter 1. Paul is in prison (4:3, 4:18), so his struggle for churches he has never visited is his prayer and anxious care for them; in 4:12 Epaphras is said to struggle for them "in his prayers".

decisions.choice: Laodicea: the larger neighboring city, about ten miles from Colossae
decisions.reason: Laodicea lay down the Lycus valley from Colossae. Paul sends greetings there and asks that the two churches exchange letters (4:13-16).

decisions.choice: all who have not seen Paul in person, the Colossians and Laodiceans among them; "their hearts" means all of them
alternatives: a third group besides the two churches
decisions.reason: ὅσοι ("as many as") widens the circle to everyone who has never met Paul; the Colossians are among them, since he has only heard of their faith (1:4, 1:9). In verse 2 he speaks of all of them as "their hearts".

decisions.choice: encouraged: strengthened and comforted
decisions.reason: παρακαλέω can mean to urge, to comfort or to strengthen. With "hearts" it means to give them courage, as in 4:8.

decisions.choice: knit together: joined into one
decisions.reason: συμβιβάζω means to bring together, unite; in verse 19 it is used of the body held together by its joints. In the Greek Old Testament it can mean "teach" (quoted in 1 Corinthians 2:16), but "in love" points to their being joined to one another.

decisions.choice: the riches of full assurance of understanding: understanding that is complete and certain
decisions.reason: πληροφορίας means fullness, and so full certainty (1 Thessalonians 1:5). Paul wants them to understand the gospel so well that no clever argument can shake them (verse 4).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the mystery of God, Christ"
alternatives: "the mystery of God the Father and of Christ"
"the mystery of God, which is Christ"
decisions.reason: Few verses have so many manuscript differences. Copyists expanded the short and slightly unusual phrase in several ways, for example to "of God the Father and of Christ". The SBLGNT has the short reading, found in an early papyrus and other important manuscripts, and it best explains how the others arose. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: Christ is the mystery
alternatives: "the mystery of God-Christ", calling Christ God
decisions.reason: Χριστοῦ stands beside μυστηρίου and says what the mystery is: Christ himself, as in 1:27 ("Christ in you").

decisions.choice: all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Christ: an echo of seeking wisdom like hidden treasure
decisions.reason: Proverbs 2:3-4 urges seeking understanding as one searches for hidden treasure. Paul says every such treasure is found in Christ, so the Colossians need look nowhere else (verse 8). ᾧ is most naturally Christ, the nearest name. "Hidden" means stored up in him, not out of reach: they are revealed to those who know him.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: never met me in person (B); never seen me face to face (R)
alternatives: have not seen my face in the flesh
decisions.reason: "In the flesh" here simply means in person.

decisions.choice: which is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out that Christ is the mystery (m8).

decisions.choice: how hard I am working and praying
alternatives: how great a struggle I have
decisions.reason: Readable says what Paul's struggle consisted of (m1).

records.source: τοῦτο λέγω ἵνα μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς παραλογίζηται ἐν πιθανολογίᾳ.
records.gloss: This I say so that no one you may delude with persuasive speech.
pieces: I tell you this so that no one will lead you astray with arguments that only sound convincing.

L.4: I say this so that no one may deceive you with persuasive arguments.

R.4: I am telling you this so that no one will fool you with clever talk that sounds true but is not.

decisions.choice: this: what Paul has just said, that every treasure of wisdom is in Christ
decisions.reason: τοῦτο λέγω looks back to verses 1-3: because all wisdom is in Christ, no one should be talked into looking for it elsewhere.

decisions.choice: deceive by arguments that win by seeming likely, not by being true
decisions.reason: παραλογίζομαι means to reason falsely and so mislead. πιθανολογίᾳ is speech that persuades because it sounds plausible. Paul does not name the teachers, but the rest of the chapter shows what they taught (verses 8, 16-23).

decisions.choice: arguments that only sound convincing (B); clever talk that sounds true but is not (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that the arguments only seem sound (m2); Literal keeps "persuasive".

records.source: εἰ γὰρ καὶ τῇ σαρκὶ ἄπειμι, ἀλλὰ τῷ πνεύματι σὺν ὑμῖν εἰμι, χαίρων καὶ βλέπων ὑμῶν τὴν τάξιν καὶ τὸ στερέωμα τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν πίστεως ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: For if indeed in the flesh I am absent, yet in the spirit with you I am, rejoicing and seeing of you the order and the firmness of the in Christ faith of you.
pieces: I may be far away in body, but in spirit I am there with you. I am glad as I see your orderly life and the solid strength of your faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.5: For even if I am absent in the flesh, yet I am with you in the spirit, rejoicing and seeing your good order and the firmness of your faith in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.5: I am not there with you in person, but I am with you in my thoughts and prayers. I am happy to see that you are living in good order and that your faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is strong and steady.

decisions.choice: in the spirit: Paul's own spirit, his heart and attention, present with them
decisions.reason: πνεύματι is set against σαρκὶ ("in the flesh", that is, in body): Paul is absent in body but present in spirit, as in 1 Corinthians 5:3. He sees them through the report Epaphras brought (1:8).

decisions.choice: good order and firmness: perhaps military words, ranks drawn up and a solid front
alternatives: ordinary words for orderliness and steadiness
decisions.reason: τάξιν was used of soldiers drawn up in ranks and στερέωμα of something firm and solid; together they may picture troops holding their line against attack. Both words also have plain everyday senses, so the picture is possible rather than certain.

decisions.choice: rejoicing and seeing: rejoicing as he sees
decisions.reason: The two participles belong together: his joy comes from what he sees.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: in my thoughts and prayers
decisions.reason: Readable says how Paul is present in spirit (m1).

records.source: Ὡς οὖν παρελάβετε τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον, ἐν αὐτῷ περιπατεῖτε, ἐρριζωμένοι καὶ ἐποικοδομούμενοι ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ βεβαιούμενοι τῇ πίστει καθὼς ἐδιδάχθητε, περισσεύοντες ἐν εὐχαριστίᾳ.
records.gloss: As therefore you received the Christ Jesus the Lord, in him walk, \v 7 having been rooted and being built up in him and being confirmed in the faith just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.
pieces: You have received {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus as Lord. So let your whole life be lived in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
with roots sunk deep in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, built up in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, made strong in the faith as you were taught, and overflowing with thanks to God.

L.6: So, as you received the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, Jesus the Lord, walk in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.7: rooted and being built up in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and being made firm in the faith just as you were taught, overflowing with thanksgiving.

R.6: You accepted {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus as your Lord. So keep living as people joined to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.7: Be like a tree with deep roots in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and like a building that keeps going up on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Keep growing stronger in your faith, as you were taught, and always be very thankful.

decisions.choice: received: took over what was handed on
decisions.reason: παραλαμβάνω is the word for receiving teaching handed down (1 Corinthians 11:23; 15:1-3; 1 Thessalonians 2:13). What they received from Epaphras was Christ Jesus himself, and verse 8 warns them not to exchange him for παράδοσιν, "tradition" handed down by people.

decisions.choice: Christ Jesus as Lord
alternatives: the Christ, that is, Jesus the Lord
decisions.reason: The second article marks "the Lord" as what they received him as: the earliest confession of believers was "Jesus is Lord" (Romans 10:9; 1 Corinthians 12:3).

decisions.choice: walk: live, conduct one's life
decisions.reason: As in 1:10, "walk" is the biblical picture for the way a person lives.

decisions.choice: rooted and built up: two pictures, a tree and a building
decisions.reason: ῥιζόομαι is in the perfect: rooted once, and staying so. ἐποικοδομέω is in the present: being built up all the time. Paul joins the same two pictures in Ephesians 3:17, and 1:23 has already spoken of a foundation.

decisions.choice: made firm in the faith: in what they believe, as they were taught it
decisions.reason: πίστει, with the article, could mean "by faith" or "in the faith". "As you were taught" suggests the faith they were taught, though trust and what it believes go together.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "abounding in thanksgiving"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "in it" (in the faith). The SBLGNT has the shorter text; the meaning hardly changes.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: let your whole life be lived in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} (B); keep living as people joined to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} (R)
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure of speech for how one lives (m3); Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: like a tree with deep roots ... like a building that keeps going up
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the two pictures (m4).

decisions.choice: thanks to God
decisions.reason: Thanksgiving in Paul is always directed to God (1:3, 1:12).

records.heading: Made full in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}

records.source: Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς ἔσται ὁ συλαγωγῶν διὰ τῆς φιλοσοφίας καὶ κενῆς ἀπάτης κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, κατὰ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου καὶ οὐ κατὰ Χριστόν·
records.gloss: Watch out lest anyone you will be the [one] carrying off as captive through the philosophy and empty deceit according to the tradition of the men, according to the elements of the world and not according to Christ;
pieces: Watch out, so that no one carries you off like captives by means of philosophy that is empty deceit. It follows human tradition and the elemental forces of the world, not {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.8: Watch out that there will not be anyone who carries you off as captives through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of {{gender:people|men}}, according to the elements of the world and not according to {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.8: Be careful! Do not let anyone capture your minds with ideas that sound wise but are empty and false. Those ideas come from what people have handed down and from the powers and rules that run this world. They do not come from {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: watch out: a real danger, from someone who may already be at work
decisions.reason: With μή ("lest") Paul uses the future indicative ἔσται ("there will be"), which makes the danger concrete, and τις ("anyone") with the article and participle points to a particular person or group he does not name.

decisions.choice: carry off as captive, like plunder
decisions.reason: συλαγωγέω is a rare word meaning to carry off as booty or to kidnap. People God rescued from the authority of darkness (1:13) could be dragged back into captivity.

decisions.choice: philosophy that is empty deceit: a particular teaching, not philosophy in general
decisions.reason: One article covers both nouns, so the second explains the first: a "philosophy" that is empty deceit. In Paul's day the word could name any system of teaching about God and how to live; Josephus calls the Jewish parties "philosophies".

decisions.choice: human tradition: teaching handed down from people, not from God
decisions.reason: παράδοσιν is teaching passed from one generation to the next. Jesus set "the tradition of men" against the command of God (Mark 7:8). It contrasts with Christ, whom the Colossians "received" (verse 6).

decisions.choice: the elemental forces of the world: the basic powers and principles thought to govern life in this world, and the rules of religion bound up with them
alternatives: the elementary principles or ABCs of religion
elemental spirits: spiritual beings ruling the world
decisions.reason: στοιχεῖον means the basic parts of something: the letters of the alphabet, the elements (earth, water, air, fire) of which the world was thought to be made, or the ABCs of a subject (Hebrews 5:12). In the thinking of the time the elements were linked with the stars and with spiritual powers. In Galatians 4:3 and 4:8-10 the "elements" go with the observance of days and months and with beings that are not gods. Here they stand beside "human tradition" and against Christ, and in verses 20-22 they go with rules about food. So the word may mean elementary religious rules or the powers thought to rule the world through them; for Paul's readers the two belonged together.

decisions.choice: not according to Christ: Christ is the measure of true teaching
decisions.reason: Twice the teaching is "according to" something human or worldly; it is not κατὰ Χριστόν. In him are all the treasures of wisdom (verse 3).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the tradition of {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general. Balanced and Readable say "human" and "people", which need no setting.

decisions.choice: the elemental forces of the world (B); the powers and rules that run this world (R)
alternatives: the elementary principles of the world
the elemental spirits of the world
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a phrase that keeps both senses of m5 open; Readable names both.

decisions.choice: capture your minds with ideas that sound wise but are empty and false
alternatives: carry you off as captives through philosophy and empty deceit
decisions.reason: Readable says what the captivity is and what "philosophy" means here (m2, m3).

records.source: ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ κατοικεῖ πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τῆς θεότητος σωματικῶς, καὶ ἐστὲ ἐν αὐτῷ πεπληρωμένοι, ὅς ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλὴ πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξουσίας, ἐν ᾧ καὶ περιετμήθητε περιτομῇ ἀχειροποιήτῳ ἐν τῇ ἀπεκδύσει τοῦ σώματος τῆς σαρκός, ἐν τῇ περιτομῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, συνταφέντες αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ βαπτισμῷ, ἐν ᾧ καὶ συνηγέρθητε διὰ τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐνεργείας τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
records.gloss: because in him dwells all the fullness of the deity bodily, \v 10 and you are in him having been filled, who is the head of all rule and authority, \v 11 in whom also you were circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands in the stripping off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of the Christ, \v 12 having been buried with him in the baptism, in which also you were raised with [him] through the faith of the working of the God the [one] having raised him from [the] dead;
pieces: For all the fullness of God's own being dwells in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} bodily,
and in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you have been made full. He is the head over every ruler and authority.

In {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you were also circumcised, with a circumcision no hand performed: the old life that the flesh ruled was stripped off you, in the circumcision that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} gives.

You were buried with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in baptism, and in baptism you were also raised with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} through faith in the power of God, who raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead.

L.9: For in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the fullness of deity dwells bodily,
L.10: and you have been filled in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who is the head of every ruler and authority,
L.11: in whom also you were circumcised with a circumcision not done by hands, in the stripping off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.12: having been buried with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in baptism, in which you were also raised with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] through faith in the working of God, who raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from [the] dead.

R.9: For everything that God is lives in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, in a human body.
R.10: And because you are joined to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, you have everything you need. He rules over every power and authority.
R.11: When you came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, you were circumcised, but not in the way people do it. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} took away your old life that was ruled by sin.
R.12: When you were baptized, you were buried with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And in baptism you were also raised with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to new life, because you had faith in the power of God, who raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead.

decisions.choice: deity: the very nature of God
decisions.reason: θεότης is an abstract noun from the word for God: being God, God's own nature. It is found only here in the New Testament. Not some of God's qualities but all the fullness of what God is dwells in Christ.

decisions.choice: bodily: in bodily form, in the human body of the risen Christ
alternatives: really, in substance, as opposed to shadow (verse 17)
as a whole body, all together
decisions.reason: σωματικῶς most naturally means in a body. The verb κατοικεῖ is the one used in 1:19, now in the present: in the risen Christ, who still has a human body, God's fullness lives. The sense "in reality" also fits the contrast with "shadow" in verse 17.

decisions.choice: filled, made complete: they share his fullness and lack nothing
decisions.reason: πεπληρωμένοι comes from the same root as πλήρωμα ("fullness"): the fullness is in Christ, and in him they are filled. They need no other power or practice to complete them (verses 16-23). The perfect says it is a settled state.

decisions.choice: head of every ruler and authority: over all the powers
decisions.reason: The same words for powers appear in 1:16 and 2:15. Here "head" means ruler: the powers are not his body, but they are under him, so there is no reason to fear or serve them.

decisions.choice: a circumcision not done by hands: a circumcision of the heart
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham (Genesis 17:10-14), and the prophets called for circumcised hearts (Deuteronomy 10:16; 30:6; Jeremiah 4:4). ἀχειροποιήτῳ ("not made by hands") marks God's own work (compare Mark 14:58). The Gentile Colossians lacked the outward sign (verse 13) but have the reality.

decisions.choice: stripping off the body of the flesh: the old life ruled by sin is put off; this is the circumcision Christ performs
alternatives: Christ's own death: "the circumcision of Christ" is the stripping off of his body on the cross
decisions.reason: ἀπεκδύσει is the noun of the verb in 2:15 and 3:9 ("you have stripped off the old self"). "Flesh" here means human nature turned from God (verse 13; Romans 8:8). "The circumcision of Christ" may be the one he performs, or his own death, when his body was stripped off; verse 12 joins believers to that death in baptism, so the two readings meet.

decisions.choice: buried with him in baptism: baptism as sharing Christ's burial
decisions.reason: Going down into the water is pictured as being buried with Christ, and coming up as rising with him (Romans 6:3-4).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: βαπτισμῷ
alternatives: the more usual noun for baptism
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have the usual noun for baptism. The SBLGNT has a rarer form, which elsewhere means washings (Mark 7:4). The meaning here is the same.

decisions.choice: in which: in baptism
alternatives: in whom: in Christ, as at the start of verse 11
decisions.reason: ᾧ can refer to baptism, just named, or to Christ, like ἐν ᾧ ("in whom") in verse 11. Buried with him in baptism and raised with him in it make a natural pair (Romans 6:4).

decisions.choice: faith in the working of God
alternatives: the faith that God's working produces
decisions.reason: ἐνεργείας τοῦ θεοῦ most naturally says what their faith rests on: God's power, shown when he raised Jesus from the dead. Faith produced by God's working is also true to Paul (1:29), but is less likely here.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: the old life that the flesh ruled was stripped off you (B); took away your old life that was ruled by sin (R)
alternatives: in the stripping off of the body of the flesh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the body of the flesh" means here (m6).

decisions.choice: everything that God is lives in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, in a human body
alternatives: all the fullness of deity dwells in him bodily
decisions.reason: Readable explains "fullness of deity" and "bodily" (m1, m2), and names Christ.

decisions.choice: you have everything you need
decisions.reason: Readable says what being filled in him means (m3).

decisions.choice: power
decisions.reason: Balanced says what God's "working" is: his power at work (compare 1:29).

records.source: καὶ ὑμᾶς νεκροὺς ὄντας ἐν τοῖς παραπτώμασιν καὶ τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν, συνεζωοποίησεν ὑμᾶς σὺν αὐτῷ· χαρισάμενος ἡμῖν πάντα τὰ παραπτώματα, ἐξαλείψας τὸ καθ’ ἡμῶν χειρόγραφον τοῖς δόγμασιν ὃ ἦν ὑπεναντίον ἡμῖν, καὶ αὐτὸ ἦρκεν ἐκ τοῦ μέσου προσηλώσας αὐτὸ τῷ σταυρῷ·
records.gloss: And you, being dead in the trespasses and the uncircumcision of the flesh of you, he made alive together you with him, having forgiven us all the trespasses, \v 14 having wiped out the against us handwritten [bond] with the decrees, which was opposed to us, and it he has taken out of the middle, having nailed it to the cross;
pieces: You were dead in your trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, but God made you alive together with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He forgave us all our trespasses.
He wiped out the bond of debt, with its decrees, that was written against us and stood opposed to us. He has taken it out of the way, nailing it to the cross.

L.13: And you, being dead in the trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made you alive together with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, having forgiven us all the trespasses,
L.14: having wiped out the handwritten bond against us with [its] decrees, which was opposed to us; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has taken it out of the way, having nailed it to the cross.

R.13: Once you were dead because of the wrong things you did. You were outside God's people, with your old sinful nature still in place. But God gave you life together with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He forgave all our sins.
R.14: It was as if we had signed a paper saying how much we owed God, because we had broken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws. That paper stood against us. But God wiped it out. He took it away and nailed it to the cross.

decisions.choice: God made you alive with Christ
decisions.reason: The last subject named is God, "who raised him from the dead" (verse 12), and it is God who raises the dead; "with him" is Christ. The same subject carries the participles that follow, through verse 15.

decisions.choice: dead in trespasses: cut off from God's life because of wrongdoing
decisions.reason: παράπτωμα is a false step, a trespass. Those who are spiritually dead cannot give themselves life; only God can (Ephesians 2:1, 2:5).

decisions.choice: the uncircumcision of your flesh: both their state as Gentiles outside God's covenant people and their old nature, not yet "circumcised" by Christ
decisions.reason: The phrase looks back to verse 11. As Gentiles they lacked the covenant sign, and their old nature, ruled by the flesh, had not been put off.

decisions.choice: forgiven us: Paul includes himself and all believers
decisions.reason: The shift from "you" to ἡμῖν ("us") includes Jewish believers like Paul: all alike needed forgiveness. χαρίζομαι is related to the word for grace: to forgive freely, as a gift (3:13).

decisions.choice: a handwritten bond of debt, like an IOU
alternatives: a general record of sins kept in heaven
decisions.reason: χειρόγραφον means a document written by hand, and in business a note signed by a debtor admitting what he owed. Here the debt is owed to God: what we owed him and failed to pay.

decisions.choice: with its decrees: the bond is made up of God's requirements that we failed to meet
alternatives: the decrees are the human rules of verses 20-22
decisions.reason: τοῖς δόγμασιν could say what the bond consisted of, or why it stood against us. Ephesians 2:15 speaks of "the law of commandments in decrees" abolished in Christ's flesh, so God's law and its demands are in view. The related verb in verse 20, "submit to decrees", then applies the point to the teachers' rules.

decisions.choice: wiped out: erased
decisions.reason: ἐξαλείφω is used for wiping writing off a page, and for blotting out sins (Acts 3:19).

decisions.choice: nailed to the cross: the debt is cancelled by Christ's death
decisions.reason: Paul pictures the bond nailed to the cross with Jesus: when he died, the debt was done away with. The Romans posted the charge against a man on his cross (John 19:19), which may lie behind the picture. The perfect ἦρκεν says it stays removed.

decisions.choice: God made you alive
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the subject (m1).

decisions.choice: the wrong things you did; sins
decisions.reason: "Trespass" now usually means going onto someone's land; Readable uses plainer words.

decisions.choice: You were outside God's people, with your old sinful nature still in place
decisions.reason: Readable says what "uncircumcision of the flesh" means here (m3).

decisions.choice: bond of debt (B); a paper saying how much we owed God (R)
decisions.reason: The word names a signed note of debt (m5).

decisions.choice: It was as if we had signed a paper ... because we had broken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws
alternatives: the bond with its decrees which was against us
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture and what the decrees were (m5, m6).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ for "him"; the title setting applies.

records.source: ἀπεκδυσάμενος τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας ἐδειγμάτισεν ἐν παρρησίᾳ, θριαμβεύσας αὐτοὺς ἐν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: having stripped the rulers and the authorities, he made a show [of them] in boldness, having led them in triumph in it.
pieces: He disarmed the rulers and authorities and exposed them to public disgrace, leading them as captives in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} victory procession by the cross.

L.15: Having stripped the rulers and the authorities, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made a public show [of them], leading them in triumph by it.

R.15: God took away the power of the spiritual rulers and authorities that were against us. By the cross {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed openly that they were beaten. It was like a victory parade, with them marching behind as prisoners.

decisions.choice: he: God, as in verses 13-14
decisions.reason: No new subject has been named since God in verse 12, so God is the one who triumphs. Some take Christ as the subject from verse 14 or 15, since the cross is his; the meaning of the victory is the same.

decisions.choice: disarmed: stripped them of their power
alternatives: stripped off from himself, like clothing
decisions.reason: ἀπεκδύομαι is the verb of 3:9 ("strip off the old self"). With the powers as its object, it means stripping them of their weapons and rank, as defeated enemies were stripped. If Christ is the subject, the picture may be of him throwing off the powers that pressed on him at his death.

decisions.choice: made a public show of them: exposed them openly to disgrace
decisions.reason: δειγματίζω means to display, often to put to shame (the same root in Matthew 1:19). παρρησίᾳ means openly, in full view.

decisions.choice: led them in triumph: the Roman victory procession
decisions.reason: θριαμβεύω is the word for a Roman general's triumph, a procession through the city in which captured enemies were marched behind the victor (2 Corinthians 2:14 uses the same verb). The powers that took people captive (verse 8) are themselves the captives.

decisions.choice: by it: by the cross
decisions.reason: αὐτῷ can refer to the cross, the last thing named, or to Christ, as "in him" does through verses 9-12. Either way the victory is won in Christ's death.

decisions.choice: the spiritual rulers and authorities that were against us
decisions.reason: Readable says who the rulers and authorities are (1:16).

decisions.choice: leading them as captives in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} victory procession (B); like a victory parade (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the picture of the triumph (m4).

decisions.choice: by the cross
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the cross (m5).

records.source: Μὴ οὖν τις ὑμᾶς κρινέτω ἐν βρώσει ἢ ἐν πόσει ἢ ἐν μέρει ἑορτῆς ἢ νουμηνίας ἢ σαββάτων, ἅ ἐστιν σκιὰ τῶν μελλόντων, τὸ δὲ σῶμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: Not therefore anyone you let judge in eating or in drinking or in respect of a festival or new moon or sabbaths, \v 17 which are a shadow of the things coming, but the body [is] of the Christ.
pieces: So no one should sit in judgment on you over food and drink, or over keeping a festival, a new moon or the sabbath.
These things are a shadow of what was coming; the substance is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.16: So let no one judge you in eating or in drinking, or in regard to a festival or a new moon or sabbaths,
L.17: which are a shadow of the things to come, but the body [belongs to] the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.16: So do not let anyone tell you that you are doing wrong because of what you eat or drink, or because you do not keep certain religious holidays, monthly feasts or sabbath days.
R.17: Those things were like a shadow that showed what was coming. The real thing is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: let no one judge you: condemn you over these matters, most likely for not keeping the rules
decisions.reason: οὖν ("therefore") draws the conclusion from verses 9-15: the bond is cancelled and the powers defeated, so no one has the right to condemn them for not keeping such observances.

decisions.choice: food, drink, festivals, new moons and sabbaths: Jewish observances
decisions.reason: Festivals, new moons and sabbaths are the Old Testament's yearly, monthly and weekly holy days, named together in 1 Chronicles 23:31 and Hosea 2:11. Rules about food and drink may come from the law (Leviticus 11) or from stricter fasting. The teaching Paul opposes seems to join such observances with other practices (verses 18, 21-23).

decisions.choice: shadow and body: the outline cast ahead, and the reality that casts it
alternatives: body: the church, the body of Christ
decisions.reason: A shadow shows the shape of something but is not the thing itself. σῶμα ("body") here means the substance, the reality (compare Hebrews 8:5; 10:1). The observances pointed ahead to what has now come in Christ. Some take σῶμα as Christ's body, the church ("let the body of Christ judge you"), but that reading strains the sentence.

decisions.choice: what was coming: future when the law was given, now come in Christ
alternatives: the world to come, still wholly future
decisions.reason: μελλόντων is present, "the things that are coming", seen from the time of the law. The reality has come in Christ, though its fullness waits for his appearing (3:4).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: the substance (B); the real thing (R)
decisions.reason: "Body" in this sense is no longer common English (m3); Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: tell you that you are doing wrong ... because you do not keep
decisions.reason: Readable says what the judging is about (m1).

records.heading: Rules that are only a shadow

records.source: μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς καταβραβευέτω θέλων ἐν ταπεινοφροσύνῃ καὶ θρησκείᾳ τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἃ ἑόρακεν ἐμβατεύων, εἰκῇ φυσιούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ νοὸς τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐ κρατῶν τὴν κεφαλήν, ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα διὰ τῶν ἁφῶν καὶ συνδέσμων ἐπιχορηγούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον αὔξει τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: No one you let disqualify, delighting in humility and worship of the angels, things which he has seen entering into, without reason being puffed up by the mind of the flesh of him, \v 19 and not holding fast the head, from whom all the body through the joints and ligaments being supplied and being knit together grows [with] the growth of the God.
pieces: Do not let anyone rob you of the prize: someone who delights in self-humbling and the worship of angels, who takes his stand on the visions he has seen and is puffed up for nothing by a mind set on the flesh.

Such a person has lost hold of the head, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. From {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the whole body, supplied and held together by its joints and ligaments, grows with the growth God gives.

L.18: Let no one disqualify you, delighting in humility and the worship of the angels, taking his stand on what he has seen, puffed up without cause by his fleshly mind,
L.19: and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, supplied and knit together through [its] joints and ligaments, grows with the growth that is from God.

R.18: Some people say that to please God you must humble yourself by going without things, and that you must worship angels. They say this because of visions they claim to have seen. Do not let them tell you that you have lost God's prize. Their pride has no good reason; it comes from their own human way of thinking.
R.19: They have let go of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, who is the head of the body. It is from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that the whole body gets what it needs and is held together, the way joints and ligaments hold a body together. So the body grows as God makes it grow.

decisions.choice: disqualify: rule against them, like an umpire denying a competitor the prize
decisions.reason: καταβραβεύω is built on the word for an umpire's award. The teacher acts as a self-appointed judge who declares that the Colossians have lost the prize. Compare 3:15, where Christ's peace is to be the "umpire" in their hearts.

decisions.choice: delighting in
decisions.reason: θέλων ἐν likely follows a Hebrew way of speaking found in the Greek Old Testament, "to delight in" (1 Samuel 18:22; Psalm 147:10). It could also mean "insisting on".

decisions.choice: humility: self-humbling by fasting and harsh discipline of the body
alternatives: the humble attitude Paul praises in 3:12
decisions.reason: The same word names a virtue in 3:12, but here and in verse 23 it goes with severe treatment of the body. In the Old Testament "humbling oneself" often meant fasting (Leviticus 16:29; Psalm 35:13).

decisions.choice: worship of angels: angels as the ones worshiped or called on
alternatives: the angels' worship: joining in the worship the angels offer in heaven
decisions.reason: θρησκείᾳ τῶν ἀγγέλων can mean worship directed to angels or worship that angels perform. Jewish writings of the time describe visionaries who joined the angels' worship in heaven, which fits "what he has seen". Worship given to angels fits Paul's stress that Christ is over all powers (1:16; 2:10) and the warning in Revelation 19:10. Either way the teaching gave angels the place that belongs to Christ.

decisions.choice: taking his stand on what he has seen: basing his claims on visions
alternatives: entering into what he has seen, as an initiate enters a shrine
going into detail about what he has seen
decisions.reason: ἐμβατεύω means to set foot on or enter, and also to go into a matter in detail. Inscriptions from the shrine of Apollo at Claros, in the same province, use it of those who "entered" after being initiated. Here the teacher builds on ἑόρακεν ("what he has seen"), most likely visions.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "what he has seen"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "not", perhaps because "entering on what he has seen" seemed hard to understand. The earliest manuscripts do not have it.

decisions.choice: puffed up for nothing by a mind set on the flesh
decisions.reason: φυσιόω means swollen with pride (1 Corinthians 8:1). νοὸς τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ is a mind that thinks in merely human ways (Romans 8:6-7): for all its spiritual claims, the teaching comes from the flesh.

decisions.choice: from whom: from Christ, the head
decisions.reason: οὗ is masculine though κεφαλήν ("head") is feminine, so Paul is thinking of Christ himself.

decisions.choice: joints and ligaments: what binds the body together and carries its supply
decisions.reason: ἁφῶν and συνδέσμων name the connections that hold a body together. ἐπιχορηγέω was used of providing what a group needed (the root is the word for paying for a chorus). The church is held together and supplied by what each part receives from Christ (Ephesians 4:15-16).

decisions.choice: the growth that comes from God
decisions.reason: τοῦ θεοῦ says where the growth comes from: God gives it (1 Corinthians 3:6-7).

decisions.choice: the head, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}; from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Christ as the head (m8); the title setting applies.

decisions.choice: rob you of the prize
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the umpire's ruling (m1).

decisions.choice: Readable first says what the teachers claim, then gives the warning
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence is long and the warning comes first; Readable puts the teachers' claims first so the warning is easy to follow.

decisions.choice: humble yourself by going without things
decisions.reason: Readable says what this "humility" was (m3).

records.source: Εἰ ἀπεθάνετε σὺν Χριστῷ ἀπὸ τῶν στοιχείων τοῦ κόσμου, τί ὡς ζῶντες ἐν κόσμῳ δογματίζεσθε· Μὴ ἅψῃ μηδὲ γεύσῃ μηδὲ θίγῃς, ἅ ἐστιν πάντα εἰς φθορὰν τῇ ἀποχρήσει, κατὰ τὰ ἐντάλματα καὶ διδασκαλίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων;
records.gloss: If you died with Christ from the elements of the world, why as living in [the] world do you submit to decrees: \v 21 Do not handle, nor taste, nor touch, \v 22 which are all for destruction in the using, according to the commandments and teachings of the men?
pieces: Since you died with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and were set free from the elemental forces of the world, why do you live as though you still belonged to the world? Why submit to rules like
"Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch"?
All these things are meant to be used up and to perish. Such rules come from human commands and teachings.

L.20: If you died with {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} from the elements of the world, why, as though living in the world, do you submit to decrees,
L.21: "Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch"
L.22: (things which are all [meant] for perishing as they are used), according to the commandments and teachings of {{gender:people|men}}?

R.20: You died with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and so you are free from the powers and rules that run this world. So why do you live as if you still belonged to this world? Why do you obey rules like
R.21: "Do not hold this, do not taste that, do not even touch it"?
R.22: These rules are about things like food, which get used up and are gone. They are only commands and teachings that people have made up.

decisions.choice: verses 20-22 are one question
alternatives: verse 21 starts a new sentence after the SBLGNT's raised dot
decisions.reason: The raised dot after δογματίζεσθε introduces the rules themselves, quoted as examples of the "decrees". The question closes only at the end of verse 22, where the SBLGNT has its question mark.

decisions.choice: if: a fact Paul takes for granted, "since"
decisions.reason: Εἰ states what is true of them: they did die with Christ (2:12; 3:3).

decisions.choice: died from the elements: died with Christ and so set free from their rule
decisions.reason: Death ends a person's obligations (Romans 6:7; 7:1-4). Having died with Christ, they are out from under the "elements" (verse 8).

decisions.choice: submit to decrees: let yourselves be put under rules
decisions.reason: δογματίζομαι comes from δόγμα ("decree"), the word in verse 14 for what was nailed to the cross. It is middle or passive: they are letting such rules be laid on them.

decisions.choice: slogans of the teachers, quoted
decisions.reason: The three commands are in the singular, like rules addressed to each person. ἅπτω is to take hold of, γεύομαι to taste, and θιγγάνω to touch even lightly: each forbids more than the last.

decisions.choice: which: the things the rules forbid, food and the like, which perish as they are used
alternatives: the rules themselves, which lead to ruin
decisions.reason: ἅ most naturally refers to what is handled and tasted. Food is used up and gone; it does not reach the heart (Mark 7:18-19).

decisions.choice: commandments and teachings of people: the words of Isaiah 29:13
decisions.reason: Isaiah 29:13 speaks of worship made of commands taught by people, and Jesus applies it to rules about food and washing (Mark 7:6-8).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: teachings of {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general. Balanced and Readable say "human" and "people", which need no setting.

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable break the question into shorter sentences
decisions.reason: The Greek question runs from verse 20 to the end of verse 22 (m1); Balanced and Readable close it after the slogans so they read easily.

decisions.choice: things like food, which get used up and are gone
alternatives: which are all for perishing in the using
decisions.reason: Readable names what the rules were about (m6).

records.source: ἅτινά ἐστιν λόγον μὲν ἔχοντα σοφίας ἐν ἐθελοθρησκίᾳ καὶ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ καὶ ἀφειδίᾳ σώματος, οὐκ ἐν τιμῇ τινι πρὸς πλησμονὴν τῆς σαρκός.
records.gloss: which things are a word indeed having of wisdom in self-made worship and humility and severity of [the] body, not in any value against [the] indulgence of the flesh.
pieces: Rules like these have the look of wisdom, with their worship that people choose for themselves, their self-humbling and their severe treatment of the body. Yet they are worth nothing for holding back the indulgence of the flesh.

L.23: These things indeed have a reputation for wisdom in self-chosen worship and humility and harsh treatment of [the] body, [but are] not of any value against the indulgence of the flesh.

R.23: These rules may seem wise. They make people invent their own ways of worship, act humble, and be hard on their bodies. But they do not help at all to stop people from giving in to sinful desires.

decisions.choice: these: the rules of verses 20-22
decisions.reason: ὅστις picks up the rules and teachings just named.

decisions.choice: have a reputation for wisdom: look wise without being so
decisions.reason: λόγον μὲν ἔχοντα, "having a word of", means having the name or the appearance of something. μὲν prepares for a "but", which follows: the look is not the reality.

decisions.choice: self-made worship: religion that people choose and invent for themselves
decisions.reason: ἐθελοθρησκίᾳ is found only here. It joins the idea of one's own will to the word for worship used in verse 18: worship invented by human choice, not given by God.

decisions.choice: harsh treatment of the body
decisions.reason: ἀφειδίᾳ means not sparing: refusing the body what it needs, as the rules of verse 21 do.

decisions.choice: of no value against the indulgence of the flesh
alternatives: of no value; they serve only to gratify the flesh
decisions.reason: πρὸς can mean "against" or "for, leading to". Read as "against", the rules cannot do what they promise: hold back the desires of the flesh. Read as "for", they are worthless and actually feed the flesh, which here would be pride (verse 18). The sentence is hard to construe, and either reading makes Paul's point that the rules fail.

decisions.choice: the flesh: human nature turned away from God
decisions.reason: As in verses 11, 13 and 18, σαρκός is not the physical body (that is σώματος in this verse) but human nature in its self-centered desires.

decisions.choice: giving in to sinful desires
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the flesh" means here (m6).

decisions.choice: invent their own ways of worship, act humble, and be hard on their bodies
alternatives: self-made worship and humility and severity of the body
decisions.reason: Readable turns the three nouns into plain actions (m3, m4).
